summary: Redwood (AE + SE) reviewed incident response, BCDR (RTO/RPO), SLA uptime targets and escalation flows with Harbor Financial (CISO + platform + legal). Key topics: SOC 2/ISO attestations, RBAC/SSO, audit logs and retention, encryption/KMS, expected RTO/RPO (Harbor to confirm), target SLA (discussion around 99.9% vs 99.95%), escalation processes (PagerDuty, severity definitions, oncall rotations), postmortem timelines and legal notice requirements. Agreed next steps to share artifacts and schedule a failover demo.
transcript: Header: 2025-06-10 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~60m | Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Lucas Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (CISO, Harbor), Aaron Kim (Head of Platform, Harbor), Priya Shah (Legal, Harbor)

00:00 - Samira: hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you taking the time. quick agenda — incident response, our bcd r controls and sla / escalation flows, leave plenty of time for q&a and any legal questions Priya, Maya, feel free to jump in at any point.

00:22 - Maya: great, thanks Samira. main thing for us is to validate RTO/RPO commitments and the escalation path — we operate under fairly tight windows for transaction replay and regulatory reporting. also want to confirm log retention and encryption details for dsp data.

00:38 - Lucas: yeah, understood. i'll walk through our IR runbook and BCDR posture; i'll also call out where SOC 2 and ISO attestations sit. quick note — some of the product names in our docs get munged by speech to text so if anything looks off in the materials, flag it and we'll clarify, eg 'kv cache' sometimes becomes 'k v cat' on the transcript.
01:05 - Aaron: one ask from infra is whether we can get a failover timeline for your private deployment option, plus how the dedicated pools are handled in the event of a region outage.

01:22 - Lucas: sure. high-level: for hosted we have multi-region redundancy with automated routing and fallback; dedicated capacity gets scheduled DR windows. for private/vpc we provide a runbook for customers to orchestrate failover — we can demo a live failover for your infra team. typical RTOs we operate to are configurable depending on contract — common defaults we've seen are RTO 1 hour with RPO 15 minutes for enterprise configs, and less stringent for standard hosted tiers. i want to be clear though: those numbers are policy-driven and we can map them to SLAs if Harbor would like commitment on a dedicated contract.

02:10 - Maya: okay that matches the ballpark. regulatory side we might push for 30 minute rpo for some flows. what's the behaviour for in-flight requests during a failover? do you preserve kv cache state or do we expect token level regen costs?

02:28 - Lucas: in-flight requests are either drained or retried depending on the severity level; we have prefix/k v cache strategies and optionally persistent cache snapshots in dedicated setups. i should note persistence of kv cache is an opt-in for dedicated/private deployments, not the default for hosted. if you need sub-30 minute rpo we'd recommend dedicated with cache snapshotting and write-ahead logs to reduce replay.
03:00 - Priya: on the legal side, our procurement folks will need explicit SLA language around uptime and credits. can you recap your standard uptime numbers and how credits work?

03:12 - Samira: yes, standard tiers: 99.9% for hosted; dedicated/enterprise can be 99.95% or 99.99% by contract. credits are pro-rated for downtime windows beyond the SLA; we can share the exact calculator. typical credit windows are cumulative per month. we'll send the SLA doc that shows the mapping — sample: 99.9% translates to ~43.8 minutes of allowable downtime per month, 99.95% is ~21.9 minutes.
03:45 - Maya: good, and how do you measure availability? is it per-region, per-route (model endpoint), token-level?

04:00 - Lucas: measured at the route/tenant endpoint level — RTT/availability from our control plane perspective. for multi-region setups availability is measured per-region and we can define global routing policies with failover. we also expose uptime metrics in the console so you can validate independently.
04:30 - Aaron: what about incident notification windows? how quickly will we be notified of Sev 1 vs Sev 2?

04:38 - Lucas: standard flows: Sev 1 — pager within 5 minutes (PagerDuty integration, SMS + email fallback), initial incident bulletin within 15 minutes, continuous updates every 30 minutes until mitigation. Sev 2 — initial notice within 1 hour, updates every 2 hours. postmortem within 3 business days for Sev 1, 7 business days for Sev 2, subject to legal review. we can customize those timelines under enterprise support tiers.
05:20 - Maya: can you define your severity levels quickly? sometimes vendors differ in what qualifies as Sev 1.

05:28 - Samira: sure — our Sev taxonomy: Sev 1 — complete service outage impacting production availability for outbound traffic; Sev 2 — partial degradation or significant feature impact; Sev 3 — localized or minor impact; Sev 4 — informational or non-production. we'll include the full list in the runbook we share.

06:02 - Priya: regarding notifications, we need written notice timelines in contract with contact points for escalation. do you have an escalation matrix including C-level contact for critical incidents?

06:16 - Lucas: yes, escalation matrix includes on-call SE, on-duty incidents manager, followed by engineering director, then VP of SRE. for legal-level escalations we include our Head of Legal and CISO. we can include direct contact methods but will redact in public docs. we'll put a sanitized escalation matrix in the packet and an internal one behind the NDA.
06:50 - Maya: audit logs — what retention do you support? and can we ship logs to our S3 or SIEM?

07:00 - Lucas: default retention is 90 days in the platform; enterprise can request extended retention up to 7 years depending on regulatory needs. we support log export to customer-managed S3 buckets, as well as real-time streaming to SIEMs via our connector (looks like eventbridge/collection to Splunk/Datadog). we'll include export instructions and sample IAM policies.
07:30 - Aaron: encryption at rest and KMS — do you manage keys or can we use our own KMS?

07:38 - Lucas: we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations for both cloud and on-prem. default is provider-managed encryption at rest with AES-256. with private deployments or enterprise agreements you can bring-your-own-key (BYOK) and we only store encrypted blobs; key rotation and audit is in customer's control via the KMS connector.
08:05 - Maya: are audit logs tamper-evident? we need chain-of-custody assurances.

08:12 - Lucas: logs are append-only in our system and we can publish signed digests for long-term tamper evidence; additionally, if you pull logs to customer S3 with object locking enabled, that meets chain-of-custody requirements.
08:35 - Priya: any certifications we can expect in the package?

08:40 - Samira: yes, we'll attach SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certificate, plus our penetration test summary and vulnerability management policy. these will be included in the security pack link I will send.
09:00 - Maya: let's talk about incident response responsibilities — who performs the remediation in a private deployment vs hosted?

09:12 - Lucas: for hosted redwood-managed infra we perform remediation and failovers per the runbook; for private deployments, we provide the runbook and assist under the support agreement — but the customer runs the failover orchestration unless you have a managed-service add-on where we operate the control plane. we can provide runbooks and run a joint drill.
09:45 - Aaron: on joint drills — do you have a standard table-top exercise and a live failover checklist?

09:52 - Lucas: yes — table-top, then staged failover tests, then a full failover. we do a pre-test checklist (backups verified, communication plan, traffic cutover plan). we will share our sample checklist and can adapt for Harbor's topology.
10:18 - Maya: one more on RPO — you mentioned optional snapshotting for KV cache. any idea on cost impact?

10:26 - Lucas: yes cost depends on frequency of snapshots and storage tier. for most enterprise customers the storage cost is a small fraction of per-token costs, but we'll provide a cost estimate in the follow-up based on your throughput numbers.
10:45 - Priya: legal redlines — we will have specific language on data residency and breach notification timelines. what is your standard breach notification window?

10:55 - Samira: standard is 72 hours for confirmed data breaches that affect customer data, but we'll surface suspected incidents earlier per the incident severity rules. we can negotiate timing; for some regulated customers we've done 48 hour windows in contract.
11:20 - Maya: do you provide a SOC 2 breach readiness checklist or an incident response pack we can plug into our internal compliance tooling?
11:28 - Samira: yes, that will be included. it includes communication templates, timeline expectations, roles and responsibilities, and sample postmortem format.
11:45 - Aaron: monitoring and alerting — can we pull raw metrics and traces? we want to hook them into our internal dashboards.
11:54 - Lucas: yup — we expose metrics via prometheus endpoints and tracing via open-telemetry collectors. you can stream them into your observability stack; we'll provide example dashboards.
12:12 - Maya: one operational question — in a degraded state, what's the recommended fallback? do you provide model fallbacks to smaller variants to keep latency low?
12:23 - Lucas: yes, smart routing can fallback to lower-cost or smaller model variants to maintain availability, that's part of our graceful degradation strategy. policies can be pinned per-route.
12:45 - Priya: regarding subpoenas/regulatory requests — who is the legal contact and how quickly do you respond?

12:53 - Samira: we have an established legal intake process and typically respond to lawful requests within the required timeline; we'll share our lawful access policy and contact points in the security packet.
13:10 - Maya: could you walk through an example timeline for a Sev 1 incident from detection to full recovery?

13:18 - Lucas: example: t0 detection (monitoring alerts), t+5m — oncall paged and initial triage, t+15m — incident commander assigned and external bulletin issued, t+30m — mitigation steps in progress (traffic reroute/failover), t+60-120m — full mitigation for common failure modes (depends on root cause), post-incident 24-72h — root cause analysis; postmortem published within 3 business days for Sev 1. actual times vary by incident. we'll include a few case studies in the materials.
14:05 - Aaron: curious about SLA credits calc — is it automatic or manual?

14:12 - Samira: we have an automated calculator but claims are submitted via support and validated; credits are then applied to billing. we can share the calculator in the docs so you can run scenarios.
14:35 - Maya: data residency — can you guarantee data at rest stays in region X?

14:42 - Lucas: yes, for enterprise contracts we support regional data residency and can pin data to specific cloud regions. for hosted multi-tenant we have region controls; for strict residency we recommend private deployment or dedicated capacity per region.
15:00 - Priya: any limitations on legal e-discovery or log access?
15:07 - Lucas: customers can request exports for e-discovery; depending on retention and export timelines there may be lead times. we'll document the process and required authorization forms.
15:30 - Maya: outstanding question — do you keep encrypted backups that Harbor can request for audits?
15:38 - Lucas: yes we keep backups; for dedicated/private we can provide audit snapshots under NDA. backup retention policies are in the runbook and can be extended per contract.

16:00 - Samira: ok wrapping up — to recap: we'll send SOC2/ISO artifacts, security pack, BCDR runbook excerpt, escalation matrix and sample SLA language; Lucas will include postmortem and incident examples and staging checklist. Harbor to confirm RTO/RPO targets and any legal redlines. schedule live failover demo week of june 23 if that works for you.
16:30 - Maya: that works. thanks everyone. one last thing — can you also share sample PagerDuty routing rules and what the escalation on-call windows look like?
16:40 - Lucas: yes, included in the runbook pack. typical on-call rotation is 1 week for SRE, 24/7 pager, follow the escalation matrix for higher levels. we can map to your existing PD policies.
16:58 - Priya: thanks, i'll coordinate legal timing. we'll aim to get redlines by 2025-06-18.
17:10 - Samira: perfect, thanks all. we'll follow up with the packet and timelines. end call.
End of transcript
